item.title: Python SMTP: Resolving Gmail Connection and Authentication Issues with smtplib
item.description:
“Python SMTP: Resolving Gmail Connection and Authentication Issues with smtplib”

When configuring Python applications to send emails through Gmail’s Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) server, developers frequently encounter connection initialization hurdles or authentication failures. Resolving these issues typically involves correct port selection, ensuring proper TLS negotiation, and, crucially in modern configurations, using the appropriate authentication methods like App Passwords instead of primary account credentials.

What are the established methods and required steps to reliably configure smtplib for sending emails using a Gmail account?

item.title: Reliable SMTP Email Address Verification Techniques and Limitations
item.description:
“Reliable SMTP Email Address Verification Techniques and Limitations”

Is it possible to programmatically ascertain whether a specific email address is active and exists on its destination mail server before sending an actual message? This query often arises in systems dealing with user registration or data hygiene, but the answer is layered with caveats due to server configurations and anti-spam measures.

Investigating Email Existence Through Direct SMTP Commands

Several techniques involve connecting directly to the destination mail server and issuing specific commands to solicit a response regarding the recipient’s status.

item.title: Resolving SMTP Error 5.5.1 Authentication Required When Sending Gmail
item.description:
“Resolving SMTP Error 5.5.1 Authentication Required When Sending Gmail”

When attempting to send emails via code using Gmail’s SMTP server, developers frequently encounter the frustrating error: The SMTP server requires a secure connection or the client was not authenticated. The server response was: 5.5.1 Authentication Required. This indicates an authentication failure, often stemming from security restrictions imposed by Google.

What are the primary reasons this specific authentication error occurs when using custom applications to send mail via Gmail SMTP, and what are the actionable remedies?
